questions.question: Write a short note on allergenic beverages. / [CO3]

questions.question: Explain the aetiology and symptoms of upper gastrointestinal tract disorders. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • Explain the aetiology and symptoms of upper gastrointestinal tract disorders. [U] / [CO2] Aetiology (Causes) – 2–3 marks ● Infection (e.g., H. pylori in gastritis/ulcer) – 1 mark ● Dietary factors – spicy foods, alcohol, irregular meals – 1 mark ● Stress and lifestyle factors (smoking, poor eating habits) – ½–1 mark ● Drug use (NSAIDs, steroids) – ½–1 mark ● Excess acid secretion / reflux (e.g., Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease) – ½–1 mark Symptoms – 2–3 marks ● Epigastric pain or burning sensation – 1 mark ● Nausea and vomiting – 1 mark ● Heartburn and acid regurgitation – 1 mark ● Loss of appetite, bloating, indigestion – ½–1 mark ● In severe cases: bleeding, weight loss – ½–1 mark

questions.question: Describe plant-source food allergens. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Describe plant-source food allergens. [U] / [CO3] ● Definition: Plant-source food allergens are allergenic substances present in foods derived from plants that can trigger immune reactions in sensitive individuals – 1 mark ● Common sources: Peanuts, Soybeans, Wheat, tree nuts (e.g., Almonds) – 1 mark ● Allergenic components: Proteins such as storage proteins, gluten (in wheat), and other plant proteins – 1 mark ● Symptoms caused: Skin reactions (rash, itching), gastrointestinal issues, respiratory problems, and in severe cases anaphylaxis – 1 mark ● Management: Avoidance of allergenic foods, proper food labeling awareness, substitution with hypoallergenic alternatives – 1 mark

questions.question: Explain macronutrient deficiencies in AIDS. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • Explain macronutrient deficiencies in AIDS. [U] / [CO1] ● Definition/Overview: In Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome, macronutrient deficiencies occur due to increased metabolic demands, poor intake, and malabsorption – 1 mark ● Causes: Reduced appetite, infections, malabsorption, drug side effects, and increased energy/protein needs – 1 mark ● Protein deficiency: Leads to muscle wasting, weight loss, weakened immunity (cachexia) – 1 mark ● Energy (carbohydrate & fat) deficiency: Causes fatigue, severe weight loss, and loss of body fat stores – 1 mark ● Consequences/Management: Leads to wasting syndrome; managed by high-calorie, high-protein diet, nutritional support, and treatment of infections – 1 mark

questions.question: Explain the dietary guidelines for managing gastritis. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • Explain the dietary guidelines for managing gastritis. [U] / [CO2] Dietary guidelines for managing gastritis ● Eat small, frequent meals – avoids excess gastric acid secretion and reduces stomach irritation (1 mark) ● Avoid irritant foods – such as spicy, fried, oily, and highly seasoned foods, which increase gastric inflammation (1 mark) ● Limit gastric acid stimulants – avoid caffeine, alcohol, and carbonated beverages (1 mark) ● Include bland, easily digestible foods – such as boiled rice, soft cereals, curd, and well-cooked vegetables (1 mark) ● Maintain healthy eating habits & lifestyle – regular meal timing, avoid skipping meals, reduce stress, and avoid smoking (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the complications of AIDS. / [CO1] [5x4 = 20] Part D Essay Each question carries 10 marks
questions.solution_html: • Describe the complications of AIDS. [U] / [CO1] Complications of Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome ● Opportunistic infections – due to weakened immunity (e.g., tuberculosis, pneumonia, fungal infections) – 1 mark ● Cancers – increased risk of malignancies such as Kaposi’s sarcoma and lymphoma – 1 mark ● Severe weight loss (wasting syndrome) – progressive loss of body weight and muscle mass – 1 mark ● Neurological complications – memory loss, confusion, neuropathy, and dementia – 1 mark ● Organ failure / multi-system involvement – chronic damage to lungs, liver, and other organs leading to death if untreated – 1 mark Part D Essay Answer any 2 questions Each question carries 10 marks
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain lower gastrointestinal tract disorders with causes and symptoms. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • Explain lower gastrointestinal tract disorders with causes and symptoms. [U] / [CO2] A. Definition (1 mark) ● Disorders affecting the lower gastrointestinal tract (small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus) that interfere with digestion, absorption, and elimination – (1 mark) B. Causes (4 marks) ● Infections (bacterial, viral, parasitic infections from contaminated food/water) – (1 mark) ● Dietary factors (low fiber diet, excessive junk food, irregular eating habits) – (1 mark) ● Inflammatory and functional disorders such as Inflammatory bowel disease and irritable bowel conditions – (1 mark) ● Other factors: stress, medications, and altered gut flora – (1 mark) C. Symptoms (4 marks) ● Altered bowel habits: diarrhea or constipation – (1 mark) ● Abdominal pain and cramping – (1 mark) ● Bloating and flatulence – (1 mark) ● Severe signs: blood in stool, weight loss, dehydration, weakness – (1 mark) D. Conclusion (1 mark) ● Early diagnosis, dietary modification, and treatment of underlying cause are essential to prevent complications – (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain biochemical and immune tests used in food allergy diagnosis. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Explain biochemical and immune tests used in food allergy diagnosis. [U] / [CO3] Biochemical and immune tests used in food allergy diagnosis A. Biochemical tests (5 marks) ● Serum histamine level test – Measures histamine released during allergic reaction (1 mark) ● Tryptase level test – Elevated in mast cell activation/anaphylaxis (1 mark) ● Eosinophil count (CBC) – Increased eosinophils indicate allergic response (1 mark) ● IgE-related biochemical estimation (total IgE) – Indicates allergic tendency (1 mark) ● Mediator release tests (e.g., leukotrienes) – Detect inflammatory mediators in allergy (1 mark) B. Immune (immunological) tests (5 marks) ● Skin prick test (SPT) – Allergen applied to skin; wheal indicates IgE-mediated allergy (1 mark) ● Specific IgE test (RAST / ImmunoCAP) – Measures allergen-specific IgE antibodies in blood (1 mark) ● Elimination diet and oral food challenge – Gold standard for identifying trigger foods (1 mark) ● Basophil activation test (BAT) – Measures activation of basophils on exposure to allergens (1 mark) ● Patch test (for delayed allergy reactions) – Detects non-IgE mediated hypersensitivity (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain malaria with causes, symptoms and types of fever. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • Explain malaria with causes, symptoms and types of fever. [U] / [CO1] Malaria – causes, symptoms and types of fever A. Definition (1 mark) ● Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites and transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito. B. Causes / Etiology (3 marks) ● Infection by Plasmodium species (e.g., P. vivax, P. falciparum, P. malariae, P. ovale ) – 1 mark ● Transmission through bite of infected female Anopheles mosquito – 1 mark ● Parasite multiplies in liver and red blood cells causing fever episodes – 1 mark C. Symptoms (3 marks) ● High fever with chills and rigor – 1 mark ● Headache, body ache, fatigue, and sweating – 1 mark ● Nausea, vomiting, anemia, and splenomegaly – 1 mark D. Types of fever pattern in malaria (3 marks) ● Tertian fever – fever every 48 hours (seen in P. vivax, P. ovale ) – 1 mark ● Quartan fever – fever every 72 hours (seen in P. malariae ) – 1 mark ● Irregular or malignant fever – seen in P. falciparum , often severe and continuous – 1 mark.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the dietary management of diarrhoea. / [CO2] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html: • Discuss the dietary management of diarrhoea. [U] / [CO2] A. Definition / Aim of diet (1 mark) ● Dietary management of diarrhoea aims to replace fluids and electrolytes, reduce intestinal irritation, and restore normal bowel function – (1 mark) B. Fluid and electrolyte replacement (2 marks) ● Increase intake of oral rehydration solutions (ORS), coconut water, clear soups – (1 mark) ● Maintain hydration to prevent dehydration and electrolyte imbalance (sodium, potassium loss) – (1 mark) C. Energy and protein intake (2 marks) ● Provide easily digestible, high-energy foods like rice, banana, potatoes – (1 mark) ● Include moderate protein sources like curd, dal water, eggs (if tolerated) – (1 mark) D. Foods to include (2 marks) ● Low-fiber, bland diet (BRAT diet: banana, rice, apple, toast) – (1 mark) ● Cooked cereals, boiled vegetables, yogurt/probiotics to restore gut flora – (1 mark) E. Foods to avoid (2 marks) ● Avoid spicy, fatty, fried foods and caffeine (irritate gut) – (1 mark) ● Avoid milk (in lactose intolerance), raw vegetables, carbonated drinks – (1 mark) F. Feeding guidelines / general advice (1 mark) ● Give small frequent meals, maintain hygiene, and gradually return to normal diet after recovery – (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
